ai.title: CLI /agent menu selects subagents via @-mention instead of switching
ai.summary: The `/agent` menu now inserts `@<agent-name>` into the input field instead of calling `resetAgent` to switch the active session. This change prevents unintended chat context switches when selecting a subagent, allowing users to @-mention agents directly. The update is limited to `npm-app/src/cli-handlers/agents.ts`, removing the `Spinner` dependency for agent selection.

eli5.text: When you open the assistant picker menu and press Enter on a subagent, it no longer jumps you into that agent's chat session. Instead, it drops an @mention of that agent into your current input box so you can address it directly while staying in your present conversation. This only affects the menu interaction in the command-line tool; selecting and chatting with agents afterward still works the same way.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.476
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.476 in `npm-app/release/package.json`. Release metadata update.

eli5.text: The software you use just rolled out a new batch of under-the-hood improvements to how its AI assistants think and work. Behind the scenes, the team swapped in newer, stronger model providers (like GPT-5 and Grok) for the helper agents that write code, judge outputs, and plan tasks, so your AI pair should be faster and more accurate at understanding what you ask. They also added a new "read-only" helper agent that can safely look around your files without changing anything, giving the main assistant better context before it starts editing. A few rough edges got smoothed too, like fixing prompt caching for certain models and preserving important context when conversations get trimmed down. These changes are all live now and bundled into the latest version, so the next time you interact with the assistant, you're already running this updated setup.

ai.title: Add GitHub links to website navbar and footer
ai.summary: Added GitHub links to the website navbar and footer components. The navbar includes a direct link with an icon and a dropdown menu item, while the footer adds the link to community and social sections. Covers `web/src/components/footer.tsx`, `web/src/components/navbar/navbar.tsx`, and `web/src/components/ui/footer.tsx`. Links point to `https://github.com/CodebuffAI/codebuff` with `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

eli5.text: The website now shows clickable links to the project's GitHub page in the top navigation bar and at the bottom of the page, with the navigation bar also featuring the GitHub logo icon. Visitors to the website will immediately see the GitHub link in both the main menu at the top and the footer section at the bottom of every page. The links open the external GitHub webpage in a new browser tab, allowing users to easily browse the project's source code, documentation, and community contributions without leaving the main website.

ai.title: README eval task count corrected to 175+
ai.summary: README.md eval description updated from 200+ to 175+ coding tasks. Aligns public copy with actual benchmark dataset size. Scope limited to README.md. No functional or code changes.

eli5.text: The public-facing description that compares how well Codebuff does versus another AI coding assistant has been quietly corrected. A number in that comparison paragraph was lowered from two hundred to one hundred seventy-five, because the actual size of the test set used to measure that comparison was miscounted. You would only notice if you read that specific sentence in the project's main overview document very closely, where the text now shows the smaller count next to a link describing the test set.

ai.title: README SDK import fix @codebuff/sdk
ai.summary: Updated README.md to import CodebuffClient from @codebuff/sdk instead of codebuff. Added npm install @codebuff/sdk instruction. Clarifies SDK package is distinct from CLI package.

eli5.text: The guide for developers using the SDK has been corrected so that it now tells people to install the right package, @codebuff/sdk, instead of importing from the wrong one named codebuff. This matters because the packages are different, so someone following the old instructions would have had trouble getting the SDK to work. If you look now, you will see the corrected install steps and import example that point to the proper package.

ai.title: Docs: update codebuff CLI usage examples
ai.summary: Web docs `large-projects.mdx`, `knowledge-files.mdx`, and `other-use-cases.mdx` updated to reflect current CLI usage. Examples show `codebuff --cwd <dir>` for directory targeting and remove explicit `<project-path>` arguments from standard invocations.

eli5.text: The help pages for this tool were rewritten so every example shows the new, simpler way to run it. Instead of typing the tool name plus a project folder path, the examples now just type the question or task, and a separate option is shown for pointing the tool at a specific folder. If you look at the guides, you will see the sample commands use fewer typed words and put the folder in a different spot, matching how the tool actually works today.

ai.title: Docs heading copy button, mobile badge, code spacing
ai.summary: Docs heading copy button reworked: desktop keeps hover-reveal, mobile tap now shows a floating badge auto-hidden after 3s (was 1.5s). Heading container split into margin/text class buckets so code snippets inside headings wrap cleanly on mobile. globals.css adds lighter inline-code styling inside h1-h6 and a max-width:767px flex-wrap rule with white-space:nowrap on code. Scope: web/src/components/docs/mdx/mdx-components.tsx, web/src/styles/globals.css.

eli5.text: When you're reading the docs on your phone and you tap the copy button that appears next to a heading, a small label now pops up showing that the link was copied and stays visible a bit longer before fading away. On a computer, the copy button still only shows up when you hover over the heading. Headings that contain inline code snippets now lay out more cleanly on narrow phone screens, keeping the code on its own line instead of getting scrunched or wrapping awkwardly.

ai.title: Markdown rendering in CLI
ai.summary: Added `MarkdownStreamRenderer` to `npm-app` using `markdown-it` and `markdown-it-terminal` to format assistant text. Updated `xml-stream-parser.ts` to route text outside tool tags through the renderer, handling smart buffering and syntax highlighting. Modified `client.ts` to adjust output spacing for new block rendering.

eli5.text: The CLI tool now displays your messages with proper formatting instead of raw text. When you're using the command-line version, text now appears with styled headings, indented bullet points, highlighted code snippets with colors, and proper spacing between sections. Previously, the assistant's replies would show up as plain text without any structure, so reading long responses with lists or code examples was harder. This makes reading conversations in the terminal much easier on the eyes.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.477 release version bump
ai.summary: The `version` field in `npm-app/release/package.json` advanced from `1.0.476` to `1.0.477` as part of the daily release-bump workflow. This commit carries no source code changes; it marks the packaging baseline for the day's accumulated updates, including GitHub links in the website navbar and footer, corrected README eval task counts, and CLI markdown rendering via `MarkdownStreamRenderer`. The version bump is metadata-only, scoped exclusively to the release manifest in the `npm-app` package.
ai.evidence: Commit bdeb2185 modifies `npm-app/release/package.json`, bumping the `version` field from `1.0.476` to `1.0.477`. The surrounding release sequence shows this is a daily version increment in the Freebuff monorepo with no code changes in this specific commit.

eli5.text: This release makes your interaction with the Freebuff assistant look and feel much better in the terminal. First, when the assistant sends you answers, they now render as nice, readable markdown text with proper formatting and syntax highlighting instead of plain, unformatted lines, so code blocks, lists, and styling appear correctly in your command-line window. Second, the project's website now includes direct links to its GitHub page in both the top navigation bar and the bottom footer, making it easier to find the source code and community resources. Additionally, the documentation has been refreshed with clearer, up-to-date usage examples and a smoother mobile experience for browsing guides. Upgrading to this version gives you a cleaner, more professional terminal output and improves how you can navigate to the project's online home and read its guides.

ai.title: Add agentrun and agentstep tables for cost tracking
ai.summary: New backend module `agent-run.ts` introduces `startAgentRun`, `finishAgentRun`, and `addAgentStep` to persist execution metadata. Database migration `0027_brown_giant_girl.sql` creates `agent_run` and `agent_step` tables to track status, credits, and step counts. `run-agent-step.ts` and `run-programmatic-step.ts` now invoke these functions to log direct and total credit usage per step.

eli5.text: The system now quietly records how much each AI task costs and how many steps it takes, storing this information as you work. When you run an agent, it starts a new entry, logs each step's credit usage, and closes the run with final totals. This data lives in two new database tables that the team can later use to show you detailed cost breakdowns per session. The change is live today, though you won't see new UI yet since it's the behind-the-scenes logging.

ai.title: Remove tool availability check in runProgrammaticStep
ai.summary: The `toolNames` validation in `runProgrammaticStep` is commented out, allowing any tool to execute via `handleSteps` regardless of agent template restrictions. This change removes the runtime error thrown when a tool is missing from the template's `toolNames` array. The modification affects the backend execution logic in `backend/src/run-programmatic-step.ts`.

eli5.text: You are an AI assistant that can now be given access to tools it previously wasn't allowed to use when running automated steps. The system used to stop execution and throw an error if a requested tool wasn't on the approved list for your specific agent setup. Now, that restriction has been removed, so any tool can run without that check blocking it. This takes effect immediately, allowing broader tool usage in automated agent workflows starting today.

ai.title: Stop loading shell config files into project context
ai.summary: Removed `loadShellConfigFiles` helper and its invocation in `getProjectFileContext`. The `shellConfigFiles` property in the returned context object is now hardcoded to an empty object `{}` instead of reading files like `.bashrc`, `.zshrc`, and `.profile` from the user's home directory. This change is scoped to `npm-app/src/project-files.ts`. Shell configuration data is no longer passed to the agent context builder.

eli5.text: When you start a coding project, the assistant used to read your personal shell setup files (like.bashrc,.zshrc) and load that information into the project context. Now the assistant no longer reads those files, so your personal shell customizations and environment variables are not included when analyzing or working on a project. You won't see these files referenced or used anymore during project setup, even if they exist on your system.

ai.title: Remove conditional check in prompt placeholder injection
ai.summary: The `formatPrompt` function in `backend/src/templates/strings.ts` now unconditionally replaces placeholders. The previous guard `if (toInject[varName])` was removed, and the replacement logic uses `toInject[varName] ?? ''`. This ensures all listed placeholders are processed, defaulting to empty strings if no value is provided.

eli5.text: When you build a reply from a template, any slot that used to be left blank if its value was missing now becomes an empty space instead. So if a piece of information wasn't provided, you'll no longer see leftover placeholder text sitting in the message; it just disappears. This happens for every slot at once, without skipping any that happen to be empty today.

ai.title: Add publisher single-owner check constraint
ai.summary: Added `publisher_single_owner` CHECK constraint to `publisher` table in migration `0028_magical_korath.sql`. Enforces mutual exclusivity between `user_id` and `org_id`, ensuring a publisher belongs to either a user or an org, but not both or neither. Scope covers database schema in `common/src/db/schema.ts` and generated migration files. Includes `unique_step_number_per_run` index on `agent_step` table.

eli5.text: Publishers in the database can now only be owned by either one user or one organization, but not both at the same time and not by neither. This prevents confusing situations where a publisher record might accidentally be linked to both kinds of owners or to no owner at all. If you looked at the publisher records, you would see each one clearly tied to exactly one owner type. A separate cleanup also ensures that step numbers within an agent run stay unique. The change is live today.
